skills.name: Research a subject
skills.description: Find relevant public sources and extract evidence for a bounded question.
skills.when_to_use: The user needs new external evidence or a source-backed comparison.
skills.when_not_to_use: The supplied material is already sufficient and only synthesis is requested.
skills.approval_policy: Read-only web operations need no external-effect approval.
acceptance: source set answers the bounded research question
examples: Research the strongest alternatives to this product.
counterexamples: Summarize the three documents I already attached.

skills.name: Summarize sources
skills.description: Synthesize supplied sources while preserving provenance and uncertainty.
skills.when_to_use: The source material is already available to the job.
skills.when_not_to_use: The user needs facts that are absent from the supplied sources.
skills.approval_policy: No external operation is implied by synthesis.
examples: Summarize these notes into the five decisions.
counterexamples: Find the latest market share numbers.

skills.name: Inspect an email thread
skills.description: Find and read the exact email thread needed for the current work.
skills.when_to_use: The request depends on an existing Gmail conversation.
skills.when_not_to_use: The user supplied all relevant email content directly.
skills.approval_policy: Reading is allowed only inside the granted mailbox scope; sending is never implied.
acceptance: thread content returned within the granted scope
examples: Check the thread with Alex and tell me what I owe.

skills.name: Draft an email
skills.description: Produce a reviewable email draft without sending it.
skills.when_to_use: The requested deliverable is an email draft or reply draft.
skills.when_not_to_use: The user wants talking points, discussion, or an immediate send.
skills.approval_policy: Draft creation is reviewable; sending requires a separate exact-payload approval.
acceptance: requested report or generated text appears inline in the email body unless the user names an existing file, requests a file format, or explicitly asks for a separate file attachment
no attachment is synthesized solely from ambiguous words such as attach or include
draft provider ID returned when a provider draft is requested
examples: Draft a reply to the latest message from Alex.

skills.name: Send an approved email
skills.description: Send exactly one previously reviewed email payload and return the provider receipt.
skills.when_to_use: The user explicitly approves sending an exact email payload already preserved in the current work lineage.
skills.when_not_to_use: The payload is incomplete, changed since approval, absent from bounded context, or the user only wants a draft.
skills.approval_policy: The grant must carry an exact-payload approval for the preserved recipient, subject, body, and attachments; any material change requires a new approval.
acceptance: the sent payload exactly matches the approved payload
the Gmail message and thread IDs are returned
examples: $send-email Send the exact draft I just approved.
counterexamples: Draft an email and send it when it looks good.

skills.name: Check a calendar
skills.description: Inspect an explicitly granted calendar window for events and conflicts.
skills.when_to_use: The user needs availability or event details.
skills.when_not_to_use: The user is asking to create or change an event without first checking context.
skills.approval_policy: Calendar reads are bounded to the granted account and time window.
examples: Check whether Tuesday afternoon is open.
counterexamples: Book Tuesday at 3pm and invite Alex.

skills.name: Propose a calendar event
skills.description: Prepare exact event details for review without creating the event.
skills.when_to_use: The user wants a reviewable event proposal.
skills.when_not_to_use: The user has explicitly approved creation of an exact event payload.
skills.approval_policy: Creating an event is a separate exact-payload approval and operation.
acceptance: event proposal includes participants, time, timezone, and purpose
examples: Propose a 30-minute call with Alex next week.

skills.name: Update a local file
skills.description: Apply a bounded edit to an explicitly granted local file.
skills.when_to_use: The requested effect is a concrete local file change.
skills.when_not_to_use: The user wants a draft in chat or an external provider change.
skills.approval_policy: Writes remain inside the path scope granted by the JobSpec.
acceptance: requested change exists at the bounded target path
target file hash verifies the saved artifact
examples: Update the release plan with this decision.

skills.name: Rewrite an artifact
skills.description: Revise supplied text under a named voice, format, or audience constraint.
skills.when_to_use: An existing artifact needs transformation rather than new research.
skills.when_not_to_use: The user needs new evidence or an external publish operation.
skills.approval_policy: A rewrite does not imply publishing or sending the result.
acceptance: rewritten artifact satisfies the requested voice, format, and audience constraints
examples: Rewrite this as a concise LinkedIn post, but do not publish it.
counterexamples: Research the history of this market.

skills.name: Capture or update an outcome
skills.description: Create one durable outcome or attach a development to a bounded existing outcome.
skills.when_to_use: The user explicitly crosses the CMD capture boundary with durable work.
skills.when_not_to_use: The utterance is a reaction, acknowledgement, repair, or discussion.
skills.approval_policy: Only bounded local CMD mutations are allowed and every mutation requires readback verification.
acceptance: canonical outcome IDs and resulting statuses read back
examples: $CMD Get Nick testing the public alpha.
counterexamples: $CMD Okay, I pressed send too fast, but all good.

skills.name: Report a blocked dependency
skills.description: Return an honest blocker with the missing input and the smallest useful next step.
skills.when_to_use: A required input, permission, connection, or external dependency prevents verified completion.
skills.when_not_to_use: The work can continue safely with available inputs.
skills.approval_policy: Reporting a blocker never expands authority.
acceptance: smallest useful next step is stated
examples: Report that Gmail is disconnected and tell me how to continue.
counterexamples: Guess the missing recipient and send anyway.
